classificationNotes: Source-draft Gargoyles are treated as an animated architectural-statue visual and encounter-production family. Claims about origin, night behavior, duty, rank, cognition, agency, personhood, and hostility remain proposals pending taxonomy review.
visualConstants: Squat crouched construction, hunched shoulders, horned beast face, clawed grip, and folded architectural wings remain recognizable.
Sandstone, granite, marble, bronze, mortar, moss, and water staining remain discrete built materials rather than flesh.
Relief carving, water-spout mouths, restrained amber seams, and pedestal fragments preserve the architectural source grammar.
Stone quality and wing architecture escalate from useless carved flaps to sovereign buttresses while load-bearing joints stay readable.
escalationAxis: Material refinement and wing architecture progress from a perched chipped ornament to a sovereign architecture that commands its own statuary court.

constructionDimensions: Family-native, non-affinity carved stone, moss and water staining, amber rune glow and amber seam glow, bronze, and water-spout architecture remain source-supported masonry, weathering, ornament, and restrained animation—not Earth, Water, Fire, or any other affinity.
Mortar, pedestal fragments, relief detail, horns, claws, and folded wings retain architectural load paths with no elemental substitution.
normal.counterplaySignal: The established perch chip, mortar joint, amber hinge seam, tracery brace, or throne-pedestal bond remains readable.
forbidden: Treating native stone, staining, or spout design as affinity evidence

constructionDimensions: Tier-safe anatomy: T1 has wings too small for flight; T2 has small wings for short stabilizing hops; T3 first gains broad functional wings and amber seams; T4 first gains marble, bronze, and window tracery; T5 alone gains buttress wings, a carved throne, and statuary attendants.
Heat-black mortar, ceramic fuel grooves, ember-cut relief channels, smoke gargles, and cooling shutters add controlled combustion while carved stone remains visible.
fire.counterplaySignal: Tier-safe anchors: T1 has wings too small for flight and exposes a perch chip; T2 small wings expose a hop hinge; T3 broad functional wings and amber seams expose a cooling joint; T4 marble, bronze, and tracery expose a brace; T5 buttress wings, throne, and attendants expose one throne vent after combustion.

constructionDimensions: Tier-safe anatomy: T1 has wings too small for flight; T2 has small wings for short stabilizing hops; T3 first gains broad functional wings and amber seams; T4 first gains marble, bronze, and window tracery; T5 alone gains buttress wings, a carved throne, and statuary attendants.
Compressed sediment laminates, crystal mortar keys, added load ribs, planted dust, and pale fracture routes engineer mineral force beyond the family's ordinary masonry.
earth.counterplaySignal: Tier-safe anchors: T1 has wings too small for flight and exposes a perch chip; T2 small wings expose a hop hinge; T3 broad functional wings and amber seams expose a loaded joint; T4 marble, bronze, and tracery expose a brace; T5 buttress wings, throne, and attendants expose one throne fault after a committed load.

constructionDimensions: Tier-safe anatomy: T1 has wings too small for flight; T2 has small wings for short stabilizing hops; T3 first gains broad functional wings and amber seams; T4 first gains marble, bronze, and window tracery; T5 alone gains buttress wings, a carved throne, and statuary attendants.
Directional pressure flutes, relief-edge vanes, debris vectors, aerodynamic mortar gaps, and a still chest keystone add engineered airflow without granting early flight.
wind.counterplaySignal: Tier-safe anchors: T1 has wings too small for flight and exposes a perch chip; T2 small wings expose a hop hinge; T3 broad functional wings and amber seams expose a still joint; T4 marble, bronze, and tracery expose a brace; T5 buttress wings, throne, and attendants expose one still throne keystone between gusts.
forbidden: Flight for T1 or sustained flight for T2

constructionDimensions: Tier-safe anatomy: T1 has wings too small for flight; T2 has small wings for short stabilizing hops; T3 first gains broad functional wings and amber seams; T4 first gains marble, bronze, and window tracery; T5 alone gains buttress wings, a carved throne, and statuary attendants.
Pressurized spout conduits, reflective fill marks, valve-cut mortar, coherent drainage channels, and mist exhaust add hydraulic force beyond native water staining and architecture.
water.counterplaySignal: Tier-safe anchors: T1 has wings too small for flight and exposes a perch chip; T2 small wings expose a hop hinge; T3 broad functional wings and amber seams expose a drain joint; T4 marble, bronze, and tracery expose a brace; T5 buttress wings, throne, and attendants expose one throne valve after pressure loss.
forbidden: Treating water staining as Water affinity

forms.battlefieldDuty: Probe approach timing with one short drop from a low architectural perch.
forms.teachingGoal: Teach that chipped sandstone feet must release together and leave the crude wing roots immobile.
forms.signatureMechanic: Chipped Drop: the perched Grotesque releases both claws for a low body slam, then scrapes back to its pedestal fragment.
forms.telegraph: Crude features tilt down and dust falls from the chipped toe that bears the perch load.
forms.counterplay: Leave the short drop lane and strike the loaded toe or tiny wing root during the scrape back.
forms.visualDelta: Small perched chipped-sandstone figure with crude features and wings too small to be useful for flight.

forms.battlefieldDuty: Repeat short wall-to-floor hops that anchor a predictable claw line.
forms.teachingGoal: Teach that moss compression and the small wing fold announce the landing claw.
forms.signatureMechanic: Mossed Hop: granite legs push from a wall while small bat wings stabilize, never sustain, one blunt-claw landing.
forms.telegraph: Weathered moss squeezes from one shoulder and the matching small wing unfolds halfway.
forms.counterplay: Cross under the unwinged side and punish the mortar gap at the landing shoulder.
forms.visualDelta: Crouched granite body, weathered moss streaks, small bat wings, blunt claws, and clear masonry joints.
forms.lowerFormInteraction: Grotesques drop into the Sentinel's landing lane; breaking its shoulder gap makes both land short.

forms.battlefieldDuty: Qualitatively pivot into a true aerial threat that traces one carved relief route before a broad-wing dive.
forms.teachingGoal: Teach players to read amber joint order and step through the final unlit relief segment.
forms.signatureMechanic: Cornice Route: amber seams illuminate shoulder, elbow, and ankle reliefs in order while broad functional wings bank toward the matching dive lane.
forms.telegraph: The upright body turns, broad wings lock, and three amber seams light along one carved relief path.
forms.counterplay: Track the seam order, cross through the unlit segment, and strike the wing hinge after the dive commits.
forms.visualDelta: Standing upright figure with carved relief detail, broad functional wings, and glowing amber seams at the joints.
forms.lowerFormInteraction: Sentinels occupy the first lit landing; breaking their wall-hop anchor erases that segment.

forms.battlefieldDuty: Control alternating aisles by opening marble-and-bronze wing tracery as a load-bearing screen.
forms.teachingGoal: Teach that bronze braces darken before each tracery aisle closes and can be broken from the open side.
forms.signatureMechanic: Rose-Window Guard: one ornate wing frames a closing aisle while the opposite tracery panel vents through a water-spout mouth.
forms.telegraph: Spired horns align with an aisle and verdigris bronze drains from the brace about to carry the marble wing.
forms.counterplay: Take the open aisle and break the darkening bronze brace before the framed wing closes.
forms.visualDelta: Marble and verdigris bronze construction, spired horns, ornate carved armor, and wings framed like window tracery.
forms.lowerFormInteraction: Guardians dive along the framed aisle; breaking its brace forces them to land and exposes their hinges.

forms.battlefieldDuty: Command an architectural boss arena where buttress wings, throne quadrants, and statuary attendants restage every learned load path.
forms.teachingGoal: Test perch chips, hop hinges, relief routes, and tracery braces while each disabled attendant removes one throne support.
forms.signatureMechanic: Arena Command — Living Elevation: the throne rotates toward one of four statuary attendants, buttress wings frame that quadrant, and the attendant performs a lower-form rule before its pedestal becomes the sovereign's exposed support.
forms.telegraph: One buttress wing settles onto the throne, the matching attendant lifts from the base, and familiar amber joints illuminate its source-form posture.
forms.counterplay: Answer the attendant's learned tell and break its pedestal bond; each lost support opens a throne quadrant and limits the sovereign's wing span.
forms.visualDelta: Architectural-scale body with flying-buttress wings, a throne carved from its own pedestal, and statuary attendants at the base.
forms.lowerFormInteraction: Grotesque, Sentinel, Guardian, and Cathedral Warden attendants each govern one elevation; solving their mechanic exposes the linked throne support.
